key_insight: LLM-BlockFE turns long unstructured text into frozen executable feature programs offline, enabling structured prediction without LLM calls at inference time.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path for industrial risk-control systems to gain value from text while keeping online latency, cost, and deployment complexity low.
method: Use an LLM-guided offline search to build feature programs block by block.
Apply block-level rollback with depth-calibrated credit to escape greedy local optima.
Run multiple interleaved search trajectories while sharing fixed direction descriptions to reduce redundant exploration.
evidence_signal: Across two public and two private datasets, the method improves AUC by 0.0069 to 0.0358 over the strongest baseline, and in five deployed applications it raises KS by 0.02 to 1.56 percentage points.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on offline search and frozen programs, performance may degrade if data distributions shift or if the discovered features are not maintained.
paper_title: Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search
